newsitem.title: USA: Bats force Washington state governor from mansion.
newsitem.headline: Bats force Washington state governor from mansion.

text.p: Washington state Gov. Gary Locke, who has been fighting a long battle against a bat colony in the governor's mansion, moved out on Friday so workers could batproof his home.
"It's hard to relax in your own home when you have bats swooping down," Locke's spokeswoman, Carolyn Duncan, said.

Since taking office in January, the governor has reported 10 bat encounters. Locke, his wife, Mona Lee, and their infant daughter, Emily, had precautionary rabies vaccinations in April after several bat sightings.
This week, bats were captured in the dining room, bedroom, laundry and living quarters of the governor's mansion, which was built in 1908.
While the family is away from the mansion, a private pest control company will try to rid the house of bats.
